args.subject: Ceramic coating cure theory for the Q3 recall
args.detail: Coat cured too fast on the line — ruled out by its lab report.
Bearing seats machined 0.4 mm undersize — the lab-supported explanation.
args.subject: Bearing seat machining theory for the Q3 recall

args.detail: Widgets compressed in transit by undersized packaging — ruled out by its lab report.

args.observation: The recall brief (http://127.0.0.1:44349/recall-brief) states exactly one of the three explanations is supported by the lab evidence, and each dossier links its own independent lab report; all three lab reports on the separate lab host were read this run.
args.excerpt: Three competing explanations for the Q3 fixture widget recall are on file. Each has its own dossier, and each dossier links the independent lab report that tested it. Exactly one is supported by the lab evidence.

metrics.answerText:
**Supported explanation: bearing seat machining** — its independent lab report found the bearing seats on every recalled batch were machined **0.4 mm undersize** ([lab report](http://127.0.0.2:45203/lab-bearing), linked from the [dossier](http://127.0.0.1:44349/theory-bearing)).

**Ruled out:**
- **Ceramic coating cure** ([dossier](http://127.0.0.1:44349/theory-coating)): the lab found "Coating cure times were within tolerance on every recalled batch" ([report](http://127.0.0.2:45203/lab-coating)) — nothing wrong with the cure.
- **Packaging compression** ([dossier](http://127.0.0.1:44349/theory-packaging)): the lab found "Packaging matched spec on every recalled batch" ([report](http://127.0.0.2:45203/lab-packaging)) — packaging couldn't have compressed the widgets in transit.

The brief confirms exactly one of the three theories is lab-supported, so the 0.4 mm undersize bearing seats are the cause.
